title: American Coleslaw
subtitle: Creamy, tangy cabbage and carrot salad
excerpt: American coleslaw is a creamy, mayonnaise-dressed shredded cabbage and carrot salad with a touch of vinegar and mustard for sharpness. It's the essential side at any BBQ or fried chicken meal. Make it an hour ahead to let the dressing soften the cabbage slightly.
sourceNotes: American coleslaw is the standard BBQ side dish across the United States, distinct from British coleslaw by the inclusion of vinegar and sometimes celery seed in the dressing.

recipe.batchNotes: Keeps well in the fridge for up to three days. Make a large batch for a BBQ.
recipe.makeAheadNotes: Make up to a day ahead. The dressing softens the cabbage pleasantly overnight.

content.text: American coleslaw is a creamy dressing on shredded cabbage and carrot. The dressing is mayonnaise-based, sharpened with cider vinegar and a little mustard. Left to rest for an hour before serving, the cabbage softens slightly and the dressing penetrates. It should be creamy but with a noticeable tartness, not sweet and gloopy.

Toss the shredded {{white-cabbage}} with {{sea-salt-fine}} and leave in a colander for 20 minutes. This draws out excess water. Rinse lightly, then squeeze out the remaining moisture in a clean tea towel. Combine the cabbage and {{carrot}} in a large bowl.

Mix {{mayonnaise}}, {{soured-cream}}, {{cider-vinegar}}, {{dijon-mustard}}, {{caster-sugar}}, and {{black-pepper}} in a bowl. Add {{celery-seeds}} if using. Taste. It should be sharp and well seasoned.
Pour the dressing over the cabbage and carrot and toss thoroughly. Cover and refrigerate for at least one hour before serving.

items.symptom: The coleslaw is watery at the bottom of the bowl
items.cause: Cabbage not salted and dried before dressing.
items.fix: The salting step removes excess moisture. Squeeze the salted cabbage firmly, press it in batches in a tea towel until as dry as possible.

items.symptom: The dressing is too heavy and sweet
items.cause: Too much mayonnaise or too much sugar.
items.fix: Reduce the mayonnaise and increase the cider vinegar to taste. The dressing should have a noticeable sharpness; American coleslaw is not a sweet dish.

items.symptom: The cabbage is still very crunchy and resistant
items.fix: Rest for at least one hour; overnight is better. The acid in the vinegar and the salt in the dressing softens the cabbage without making it limp.

items.cause: Dressing underseasoned before adding to the cabbage.
items.fix: Season the dressing to taste before it goes on the cabbage. Once the cabbage is mixed in, it dilutes the dressing. The dressing should taste a little too sharp and salty on its own.

content.text: Coleslaw is the standard side at American BBQs, alongside potato salad and corn on the cob. The word comes from the Dutch koolsla, meaning cabbage salad. The dish has been in American cookbooks since the 18th century. The mayonnaise-dressed version became the default in the 20th century.
